answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making endorsements scarce and punishable. Each established identity can sponsor only a few newcomers, and each sponsorship locks part of the sponsor's balance. When one fake sparrow account is caught, the penalty burns the backer's stake too. Every endorsement thus becomes a costly signal that a real actor is willing to risk capital on that newcomer. An attacker mass-registering clones gains nothing: a hundred identical plumes without honest sponsors carry zero weight, and each exposed puppet drains the capital staked behind it.
